column5: fact   (ALL PRODUCT, PREVALENCE, ACCOUNT AND ACCESS FACTS BELOW ARE FICTIONAL, ILLUSTRATIVE DEMO DATA)
Product: Cardivex (fictional demo brand), a once-daily oral therapy that is one of the four guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) classes for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).

Approved indication: adults with chronic HFrEF (LVEF 40% or less) to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization, used alongside other GDMT. Use outside this population is off-label.

Approved safety info (demo): monitor potassium and renal function at initiation and after dose changes; avoid in patients with a history of angioedema; caution in symptomatic hypotension. Refer clinical dosing questions to the full prescribing information.

Illustrative demo data: the territory covers the Mississippi Delta and rural Alabama. Heart failure prevalence is about 1.5x the national average; adult hypertension about 45%. Only about 1 in 4 eligible HFrEF patients is on all four GDMT classes. Fewer than 1 cardiologist per 25,000 residents; most HFrEF patients are managed by PCPs and NPs. Typical drive time between practices is 45-90 minutes.

PCP / NP talk track (simple, safe, easy to start): focus on starting one more GDMT class at low dose in a stable patient, a simple monitoring plan (potassium and creatinine at 1-2 weeks), and when to refer to cardiology. Avoid titration detail and outcomes tables.

Cardiologist talk track (titration, sequencing, outcomes): rapid sequencing of the four GDMT classes, titration targets, the approved cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization outcomes, and shared-care handoff with PCPs.
Community Health Center talk track: team-based GDMT protocol for nurses and pharmacists, standing orders for lab monitoring, and how patients can access 340B pricing and patient assistance.
Medicaid formulary (demo): Mississippi and Alabama Medicaid cover Cardivex with a simple prior-authorization form for HFrEF; typical approval time 2 business days. Commercial plans mostly Tier 3.
340B (demo): participating 340B community health centers and their contract pharmacies in the territory can access reduced pricing. Pharmacy list is maintained by the Market Access team.

Patient assistance (demo): the company patient-assistance program offers help for uninsured or underinsured patients who meet program income criteria. The rep describes the program; the program decides eligibility.

Off-label or unsolicited clinical questions go to Medical Information (1-800-000-0200, fictional). Formulary or contracting questions go to Market Access. Possible adverse events must be reported per SOP within 24 hours.

Demo status: Family-medicine PCP in a rural Delta town. Roughly 140 HFrEF patients, an estimated 20% on all four GDMT classes. Practice is 70 minutes from the nearest cardiologist. Medicaid-heavy panel. Open to adding a fourth GDMT class but worried about potassium monitoring.
Demo status: Nurse practitioner at a rural clinic, about 60 HFrEF patients, GDMT use unknown. Runs a nurse-led heart failure clinic one day a week. Needs a simple protocol.
Demo status: Cardiologist at a regional hospital, about 300 HFrEF patients, an estimated 45% on all four GDMT classes. Receives referrals from 12 PCPs. Interested in sequencing and outcomes data.
Demo status: Primary care physician, small practice, about 40 HFrEF patients, an estimated 15% on all four GDMT classes. Rarely sees reps; prefers a 10 minute visit booked in advance.

Demo status: 340B-eligible community hospital with a heart failure outpatient clinic; contract pharmacy in the county; about 200 HFrEF patients, GDMT use unknown. Account type: Community Health Center / hospital clinic.
